subject: Information Theory
title: Bandwidth vs SNR Tradeoff
description: One-minute skill: Bandwidth vs SNR Tradeoff.

hook.text: You can whisper slowly in a wide hallway or shout quickly through a narrow pipe. Both carry the same information.

buildup.text: Shannon's formula reveals a fundamental tradeoff: you can trade bandwidth for SNR and vice versa.

discovery.text: Spread-spectrum exploits this: use enormous bandwidth at very low power. GPS signals are weaker than background noise.

twist.text: Narrowband systems need high power to achieve the same capacity. Wideband systems can whisper and still deliver.

climax.text: This tradeoff shapes every wireless standard. 5G uses wider bands; satellite links use higher power.

punchline.text: Wide and quiet, or narrow and loud. Same data.

quiz.question: What does Shannon's formula show about bandwidth and SNR?
options: You can trade one for the other to maintain capacity
